question.text: An individual investor redeems Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) upon maturity. What is the tax treatment of the capital gains arising on such redemption?

answer.text: Taxable as long-term capital gains at 20% with indexation benefit
Taxable as long-term capital gains at 12.5% without indexation
Fully exempt from capital gains tax
Taxable as short-term capital gains at applicable slab rates

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook treats redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) by an individual as not amounting to a transfer, so no capital gains arise on such redemption. That is why redemption by an individual investor is exempt from capital gains tax. The Trap: Options A, B and D apply LTCG/STCG rates that would be relevant for a taxable transfer; here the individual redemption is treated as non-transfer, so capital gains do not arise in the first place. Note: A secondary-market transfer of SGBs is treated as a taxable transfer, and the periodic interest received on SGBs remains taxable as interest income.
